'''Fanghua Lin''' ({{zh|t=林芳華|p=Lín Fānghuá}}; born March 11, 1959), also written as '''Fang-Hua Lin''', is a Chinese-born American [[mathematician]]. He is currently the Silver Professor at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]] at [[New York University]]. He applies rigorous analysis to nonlinear systems and is a leader in this field.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://silverdialogues.fas.nyu.edu/page/Fang_Hua_Lin |title=The Silver Dialogue |access-date=2008-01-17 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070712024559/http://silverdialogues.fas.nyu.edu/page/Fang_Hua_Lin |archive-date=2007-07-12 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2025.<ref>https://www.nasonline.org/news/2025-nas-election/</ref>

==Biography==
Lin was born in 1959 in [[Ningbo]], [[Zhejiang]], China, and graduated from the Department of Mathematics of [[Zhejiang University]] in 1981. He went to the United States to obtain his PhD from the Department of Mathematics at the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1985. From 1985 to 1988, he was an instructor at the Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences at New York University. Then he went to the [[University of Chicago]], and was a full professor there from 1988 until 1989. In 1989, he started his professorship at New York University. He was awarded the Silver Professorship at the Courant Institute.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cms.zju.edu.cn/news.asp?id=646&ColumnName=news&Version=|title=陈省身奖获得者林芳华教授简介|last=|first=|date=2004-12-23|website=Zhejiang University|archive-url=|archive-date=|url-status=|access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://math.nyu.edu/people/profiles/LIN_Fang-Hua.html|title=Fang-Hua Lin|last=|first=|date=|website=New York University|archive-url=|archive-date=|url-status=|access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref>

Lin made substantial contributions in [[Ginzburg–Landau theory]].<ref name="Landau"/>

==Awards and honors==
* 1989–1991, [[Sloan Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Research Fellowship]]
* 1989–1994, [[Presidential Young Investigator Award]]
* 1990, invited speaker, [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], Kyoto<ref>{{cite book|author=Lin, Fang-Hua|chapter=Static and moving defects in liquid crystals|title=''In:'' Proceedings of the international congress of mathematicians (Kyoto, 1990)|publisher=Math. Soc. Japan|year=1991|volume=I|edition=2nd|pages=1165–1171}}</ref>
* 1999, Ordway Chair Visiting Professor, University of Minnesota
* 2002, [[Bôcher Memorial Prize]], by [[American Mathematical Society]] for fundamental contributions to our understanding of the Ginzburg-Landau equations<ref name="Landau">{{cite journal | last=Hua Lin | first=Fang | title=Some dynamical properties of Ginzburg-Landau vortices | journal=Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics | volume=49 | issue=4 | date=1996 | issn=0010-3640 | doi=10.1002/(SICI)1097-0312(199604)49:4<323::AID-CPA1>3.0.CO;2-E | pages=323–359}}</ref>
* 2004, [[Shiing-shen Chern|Shiing-shen Chern Prize]]
* 2004, fellow, [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]<ref>[http://news.163.com/2004w05/12552/2004w05_1084520006195.html NetEase: 华裔教授林芳华和田刚当选美国艺术科学院院士]</ref>
* 2014, fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]]<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2014-12-17</ref>
* 2022, [[SIAM Fellow]], "for significant contributions to our understanding of the properties of solutions throughout nonlinear partial differential equations"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/siam-announces-class-of-2022-fellows|title=SIAM Announces Class of 2022 Fellows|date=March 31, 2022|work=SIAM News|access-date=2022-03-31}}</ref>
